title: ST-MTM: Masked Time Series Modeling with Seasonal-Trend Decomposition for Time Series Forecasting

problem.claim: Forecasting complex time series with intricate temporal variations is important and challenging across industrial applications.

gap.claim: Raw-series masking can ignore inherent semantic structure and cause masked time-series models to learn spurious temporal patterns.

contributions.claim: ST-MTM is a masked time-series modeling framework that uses seasonal-trend decomposition and component-specific masking.
The framework applies period masking to seasonal components and sub-series masking to trend components.
ST-MTM adds a contrastive learning task to enhance contextual consistency among masked seasonal representations.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the component-aware seasonal-trend masking method as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the proposed masking method provides an effective pre-training task for learning intricate temporal variations and dependencies.
The authors report consistently superior forecasting performance compared with existing masked modeling, contrastive learning, and supervised forecasting methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Complex time-series forecasting is important but difficult.
Masked time-series modeling reconstructs masked segments from unmasked segments to model temporal dependencies.
Masking raw time series can overlook semantic structure created by multiple components and encourage spurious pattern learning.
ST-MTM addresses entangled patterns through seasonal-trend decomposition and component-specific masking, supplemented by contrastive learning.
The authors report effective pre-training and superior forecasting performance against several existing method categories.

source_observation.claim: Raw-series masking may ignore semantic structure arising from multiple time-series components.

interpretation.claim: Self-supervised objectives may be better aligned with structured representations when the data contains entangled components.

application.claim: For forecasting data with separable seasonal and trend behavior, consider component-aware decomposition and masking strategies.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach benefits time series without meaningful seasonal-trend structure.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative performance differences are not specified.
The decomposition procedure, model architecture, training configuration, and computational costs are not specified.
Limitations and failure cases are not reported.
